about: Applied by scripts/build_course_files.js on top of the workbook, which stays as it is. labels: a verb card's tense name on the Spanish face, put in English for the English speaker; {x} stands for any word and is carried across. cards: per Card ID, meaning (the front of a Rule card in English, shown large at the top of its back), remember (with a meaning beside each Spanish word) or target. remember (whole lines): a Remember line as the workbook has it, mapped to the same line with English beside each Spanish word, applied to every card that carries it.

remember.Casual words (¿qué onda?, órale, no manc: Casual words (¿qué onda? = what's up?, órale = OK, come on, no manches = no way) are for friends only.
bien (well) and mal (badly) never change form.
remember.From llamarse, literally \"I call myself: From llamarse (to be called), literally "I call myself".
The little word de (of, from) goes first.
lo siento (I'm sorry) comes from sentir, to feel.
A command form of pasar (to come in, to pass).
puede (you can) + infinitive, from poder (to be able to).
remember.nos vemos is from verse, to see each oth: nos vemos (see you) is from verse, to see each other.
remember.The verb ending shows the person, so Spa: The verb ending shows the person, so Spanish often drops the pronoun: Soy de Oregon (I'm from Oregon).
remember.Most -ma words are still feminine: la ca: Most -ma words are still feminine: la cama (the bed). Other exceptions met so far: el mapa (map), el día (day), la foto (photo), la moto (motorbike). agua (water) is feminine but takes el.
remember.Same for both genders: especial, natural: Same for both genders: especial, natural, popular, tropical, diferente, excelente, interesante, importante, terrible, útil (useful), común (common).
remember.A few common ones can go first: buen, ma: A few common ones can go first: buen (good), mal (bad), próximo (next).
remember.idea is feminine; every -ma word here is: idea is feminine; every -ma word here is masculine (el tema, the topic; el idioma, the language).
grande (big) stays the same for both genders.
Use viejo (old) for things, mayor (older) for people.
fácil (easy) is for things, not people.
remember.A person: only after a noun, un cliente: A person: only after a noun, un cliente frecuente (a regular customer).
remember.próximo matches its noun: la próxima sem: próximo (next) matches its noun: la próxima semana (next week).
✗ Soy una maestra. (Say Soy maestra, I'm a teacher.)
remember.Seen: el gusto es mío (L1), la tuya (L5): Seen: el gusto es mío, the pleasure is mine (L1); la tuya, yours (L5).
remember.Always la pareja, even for a man, so the: Always la pareja (the partner), even for a man, so the describing word stays feminine.
remember.persona is always feminine; gente is sin: persona (person) is always feminine; gente (people) is singular: la gente es… (people are…)
No article after ser: not una maestra (a teacher).
contador (accountant) comes from contar, to count.
carrera (career) can also mean a race.
Use mayor (older), not viejo (old), for older people.
remember.fuerte also means a strong coffee or a l: fuerte (strong) also means a strong coffee or a loud noise.
remember.With estar, rico means tasty. Before a n: With ser, rico means rich. With estar, rico means tasty. Before a name, pobre = poor thing.
remember.Correct with ser or estar; está casada i: Correct with ser or estar; está casada (she's married) is the everyday way.
remember.content@ goes with estar; feliz works wi: content@ (happy) goes with estar; feliz (happy) works with both.
remember.Before a masculine singular noun: buen,: Before a masculine singular noun: buen (good), mal (bad).
remember.Understand them; not practice words. A v: Understand them; not practice words. A vendor may call a customer güero (blondie, fair one).
remember.DOCTOR uses. One thing es, more than one: DOCTOR uses. One thing es (is), more than one son (are).
remember.mil never takes un. ✗ doscientos y cincu: mil (thousand) never takes un (a). ✗ doscientos y cincuenta (two hundred and fifty)
remember.Where an event takes place uses ser: La: Where an event takes place uses ser: La fiesta es en mi casa (The party is at my house).
remember.Before a noun uno becomes un or una: un: Before a noun uno (one) becomes un or una (a): un taco, una plaza (a square).
remember.16 to 19 fuse into one word: diez y seis: 16 to 19 fuse into one word: diez y seis → dieciséis (sixteen).
remember.21 to 29 are one word. Before a noun: ve: 21 to 29 are one word. Before a noun: veintiún, veintiuna (twenty-one).
remember.31 to 99: tens + y + ones: treinta y uno: 31 to 99: tens + y (and) + ones: treinta y uno (thirty-one).
remember.Hundreds match the noun: doscientos peso: Hundreds match the noun: doscientos pesos (two hundred pesos), doscientas casas (two hundred houses).
remember.The three that break the pattern (not ci: The three that break the pattern (500 is quinientos, not cincocientos).
remember.mil never takes un. y joins only tens an: mil (thousand) never takes un (a). y (and) joins only tens and ones: doscientos cincuenta y tres (253).
Months are lowercase and take en (in).
remember.Seasons take en. Spring is the only femi: Seasons take en (in). Spring is the only feminine one.
remember.In general. Mexico says en la, not por l: In general. Mexico says en la (in the), not por la.
Minutes: y + number: son las dos y diez (it's ten past two).
aquí (here), allí, ahí (there), allá (over there) never take de (of).
ropa (clothes) is singular: la ropa está (the clothes are).
remember.They agree like any describing word, exc: They agree like any describing word, except de pie (standing), which never changes.
remember.A person uses tener: tengo frío, tengo c: A person uses tener: tengo frío (I'm cold), tengo calor (I'm hot).
remember.todavía and ya usually come before estar: todavía (still) and ya (already, now) usually come before estar.
With a place after: cerca de (near), lejos de (far from).
remember.With a place after: adentro de, afuera d: With a place after: adentro de (inside), afuera de (outside).
remember.Never changes. Don't confuse it with sol: Never changes. Don't confuse it with sol@, which means alone.
remember.muy is neutral; demasiado means it's a p: muy (very) is neutral; demasiado (too much) means it's a problem.
a (to) + el (the) always squeezes into al.
remember.un café con leche · un café sin leche: un café con leche (coffee with milk) · un café sin leche (coffee without milk)
remember.Most place words link with de; de + el =: Most place words link with de (of); de + el = del (of the).
entre (between) links with y (and), not de (of).
✗ Soy treinta. ✗ Estoy treinta años. (I'm thirty is Tengo treinta años.)
✗ Tengo la sed. (I'm thirsty is Tengo sed.)
A little: un poco de frío (a little cold).
Never say estoy caliente about yourself: it means aroused, not warm.
agua (water) is feminine but takes el: el agua.
medicina (medicine) is also the field of study.
With tener, no article: tengo fiebre (I have a fever).
remember.In Mexico el mandado is above all the fo: In Mexico el mandado (the errands) is above all the food shopping.
remember.Mexicans carry two apellidos and go by t: Mexicans carry two apellidos (last names) and go by the first one.
remember.No article. hambre and sed are feminine:: No article. hambre (hunger) and sed (thirst) are feminine: mucha hambre (very hungry).
remember.Masculine: mucho frío. A thing está frío: Masculine: mucho frío (very cold). A thing está frío (is cold).
sueño (sleepiness) is masculine; prisa (hurry) is feminine.
Keep the que (tener que = to have to). Only tener changes.
remember.PASO uses: possession, age, sensation, o: PASO uses: possession, age, sensation, obligation (tener que, to have to).
remember.✗ ¿Dónde el baño está?: ✗ ¿Dónde el baño está? (Say ¿Dónde está el baño?, where's the bathroom?)
remember.✗ ¿Dónde eres de?: ✗ ¿Dónde eres de? (Say ¿De dónde eres?, where are you from?)
✗ Nadie no está. · ✗ Tengo nada. (Say No está nadie, nobody's here · No tengo nada, I don't have anything.)
✗ No tengo algo. (Say No tengo nada, I don't have anything.)
remember.algún, ningún before masculine; alguna,: algún (some), ningún (no) before masculine; alguna, ninguna before feminine.
remember.A person, thing or place uses estar: ¿Dó: A person, thing or place uses estar: ¿Dónde está el baño? (Where's the bathroom?)
remember.✗ el este libro. (el libro este exists i: ✗ el este libro (the this book). (el libro este exists in casual speech, often with a negative tone.)
remember.A short person is baj@; short hair is el: A short person is baj@ (short); short hair is el pelo corto.
que se mejore (get well soon) is a fixed wish form.
remember.no te preocupes is a fixed negative comm: no te preocupes (don't worry) is a fixed negative command.
remember.Goes before the noun and takes the place: Goes before the noun and takes the place of el / la (the).
remember.In Mexico ese often does the job of aque: In Mexico ese (that) often does the job of aquel (that over there) too.
Four forms: rojo, roja, rojos, rojas (red).
Two forms: one and more (azul · azules, blue). Not ripe yet: está verde (it's green).
remember.Hair uses tener + el pelo. chino is curl: Hair uses tener (to have) + el pelo (the hair). chino is curly in Mexico.
remember.mal (how you are) never changes; malo, m: mal (how you are) never changes; malo, mala, malos, malas (bad) matches its noun.
remember.Same pattern with caro, pesado, ligero,: Same pattern with caro (expensive), pesado (heavy), ligero (light), lento (slow), oscuro (dark), nervioso (nervous), tranquilo (calm), ruidoso (noisy).
remember.sé is from saber. Learn no sé as a whole: sé (I know) is from saber (to know). Learn no sé (I don't know) as a whole phrase for now.
de + el = del: depende del día (it depends on the day).
remember.Just sí or no after creo que, no extra w: Just sí (yes) or no after creo que (I think), no extra words.
claro (sure) alone is the short version.
remember.In Mexico you hear con gusto as often as: In Mexico you hear con gusto (gladly) as often as de nada (you're welcome), especially in shops.
remember.Add de su parte for extra politeness: mu: Add de su parte (on your part) for extra politeness: muy amable de su parte (very kind of you).
The answer to any question with ya (already, yet).
remember.sale is friendly and casual; está bien w: sale (OK, sure) is friendly and casual; está bien (all right) works with anyone.
remember.no pasa nada is the kind reply to an apo: no pasa nada (no problem) is the kind reply to an apology.
remember.You already saw these in the stories: tr: You already saw these in the stories: trabaja (works), estudia (studies), llama (calls).
remember.Seen in Lesson 3: Gabriel vive en Guadal: Seen in Lesson 3: Gabriel vive en Guadalajara (Gabriel lives in Guadalajara).
remember.Frequency words usually go before the ve: Frequency words usually go before the verb or at the end. After the verb, nunca (never) needs no: No manejo nunca (I never drive).
remember.Fixed phrases from dedicarse. Politer th: Fixed phrases from dedicarse (to do for a living). Politer than asking ¿cuál es tu trabajo? (what's your job?)
remember.Estoy jubilad@ is also common. Both are: Estoy jubilad@ (I'm retired) is also common. Both are correct.
remember.No un after trabajo de: Trabajo de meser: No un (a) after trabajo de: Trabajo de mesero (I work as a waiter).
remember.negocio also means a small shop: el nego: negocio (business) also means a small shop: el negocio de la esquina (the corner shop).
empresa (company) is the most common word.
remember.reunión also works; junta is the office: reunión (meeting) also works; junta (meeting) is the office word in Mexico.
ganar (to earn) also means to win.
remember.cada never changes: cada día, cada mes,: cada (each, every) never changes: cada día, cada mes, cada año (every day, month, year).
remember.Same meaning. todos los días is more com: Same meaning. todos los días (every day) is more common in speech. todo agrees: todas las semanas (every week).
remember.seguido is the everyday Mexican word; a: seguido (often) is the everyday Mexican word; a menudo (often) sounds more bookish.
remember.los + day = every: los martes, los fines: los + day = every: los martes (on Tuesdays), los fines de semana (on weekends).
remember.-ar verb. After tener que, hay que and p: -ar verb. After tener que (have to), hay que (one has to) and para (to, in order to) it never changes.
remember.-er verb. After tener que, hay que and p: -er verb. After tener que (have to), hay que (one has to) and para (to, in order to) it never changes.
remember.-ir verb. After tener que, hay que and p: -ir verb. After tener que (have to), hay que (one has to) and para (to, in order to) it never changes.
remember.Later you'll meet more: pongo, salgo, ve: Later you'll meet more: pongo (I put), salgo (I go out), vengo (I come).
Seen in Lesson 1: no entiendo (I don't understand).
